The County has a need to continue to provide for a just, effective, efficient, and economical
system of providing legal counsel for persons charged with criminal offenses who claim that they
are financially unable to retain private counsel (indigent).
The Attorney is willing to provide defense representation to individuals determined by the
County to be indigent and charged with criminal offenses that would subject them to possible
incarceration. The Attorney will provide this representation in accordance with the rules, laws, and
standards set out by the Michigan Indigent Defense Commission (MIDC).
THEREFORE, it is agreed between the County and the undersigned Attorney, as follows:
This Agreement supersedes any and all prior agreements between the County and the Attorney
concerning representation of indigent defendants. The term of this Agreement begins October 1,
2026, and continues through September 30, 2027, unless terminated earlier under Section 7.
The Attorney shall comply with all of the standards set forth by the MIDC and the Michigan Rules
of Professional Conduct and shall maintain Professional Liability Insurance of at least One
Hundred Thousand Dollars under this Agreement. The Attorney shall be regarded in all ways as
an independent contractor, and the County shall not be liable for any damages or injuries arising
out of the Attorney's performance of duties under this Agreement. The Attorney shall be
responsible for the preparation and submission of 1099 forms or other tax-related forms on the
In representing a client, the attorney assigned shall give priority to the obligations under the
Agreement in scheduling appearances, and shall:
• Be on time and prepared for all court proceedings.
• Promptly identify and resolve conflicts of interest.
St. Joseph County Indigent Defense Agreement
• Continuously represent the client in the proceeding, except for isolated, unusual, or
unexpected circumstances as approved by the assigned judge.
• Conduct an initial meet with the client within three days of arraignment if in custody;
• Meet with the client in private, review charges, provide discovery, explain defenses, and
• File and litigate appropriate motions and complete discovery.
• Prepare the client for plea, trial, and sentencing as required.
The term “Criminal Offender” and “Defendant” as used in this Agreement means persons
determined to be indigent, 18 years of age or older charged with an offense under the statutes of
the State of Michigan or ordinances of the Municipal Corporations within St. Joseph County,
including those charged with probation violations. The term shall not include civil contempt cases
such as non-support or violation of restraining orders.
The Attorney agrees to provide representation at Friend of the Court show cause hearings and PPO
violation hearings without additional compensation. The Attorney shall provide representation
when appointed by the Chief Public Defender of S. Joseph County. The Chief Public Defender
will provide a notice of appointment to the courts and Attorney specifying any cases the Attorney
Except as provided below, the Attorney shall be responsible for complete representation in all
proceedings through disposition by sentence or dismissal, including meritorious appeals to Circuit
Court, even if disposition extends beyond the termination date of this Agreement.
• The Attorney shall be compensated only for actual time worked and properly documented
under this Agreement. No advance, retainer, minimum payment, duty-week prepayment,
or other guaranteed payment is due.
• The Attorney shall track all billable time on the approved spreadsheet, identify the
applicable case type, and submit an invoice and completed timesheet at the end of each
month after the work is performed.
• The County shall pay the Attorney for approved, properly documented hours actually
worked during the preceding month at the applicable hourly rate stated below.
• The County has no obligation to pay for time not actually worked, time not properly
documented, or work performed after the Attorney assumes judicial office.
• The Attorney will be paid per MIDC Standards at the following hourly rates:

• The Chief Public Defender may audit timesheets to ensure accuracy and has final say in
The Attorney is an independent contractor. The County shall not provide facilities, benefits, or
insurance and shall not be liable for taxes, insurance, or other obligations incurred by the Attorney.
This Agreement is terminable as to the Attorney:
• Upon 30 days’ written notice by either party;
• Upon 10 days’ notice if Attorney becomes unable to perform due to disability for 20 days;
• Upon issuance of a public disciplinary order against the Attorney; or
• Automatically, immediately before the Attorney assumes judicial office in January 2027.
This Agreement is subject to all standards adopted by the Michigan Indigent Defense Commission,
• Standard 4 – Counsel at First Appearance and Other Critical Stages
